title: Food, Potlucks and Tips
intro_es: Comer es la forma más sabrosa de entender Canadá: costumbres, platillos y cuánto dejar de propina.
paragraphs: Food is a great way to learn about a new country. Canada is very multicultural, so in Edmonton you can find food from almost everywhere: Vietnamese soup, Indian curry, Lebanese shawarma and, yes, Mexican tacos too. Edmonton also has a big Ukrainian community, so many families love perogies, small dumplings filled with potato and cheese.

Some Canadian classics are worth trying. Poutine is french fries with cheese curds and hot gravy. Butter tarts are small, sweet pastries. In Alberta, people are proud of their beef, and in summer many families have barbecues in the backyard. Breakfast is often quick: coffee, toast, cereal or eggs. Lunch is usually light, and dinner is the main meal, often between five and seven o'clock.

Soon you may get an invitation to a potluck. At a potluck, every guest brings one dish to share. It is a common way to eat together at work, at church or with neighbours. Bring something easy to serve, like a salad, a dessert or rice. It is a good idea to tell people what is in your dish, because some guests have allergies or don't eat meat.

At restaurants with table service, people expect a tip. Most people leave about 15 to 20 percent of the bill before tax. When the server brings the payment machine, you can choose the percentage on the screen. At a counter, a tip is optional. Also remember that the prices on the menu usually do not include tax.
Don't be shy about sharing your own food culture. Bring tamales to the next potluck, and you will probably make new friends!

options: Canadians do not like to try food from other countries.
Restaurants in Canada are more expensive than in Mexico.
Food in Canada is diverse, and knowing customs like potlucks and tipping helps you fit in.
main_idea.why_es: El texto presenta la variedad de comida en Edmonton y explica costumbres útiles: potlucks y propinas.

questions.q: What do you do at a potluck?
options: Cook for the host in their kitchen
questions.why_es: En un potluck cada invitado lleva un platillo para compartir con todos.

questions.q: How much do people usually tip at a restaurant with table service?
options: About 15 to 20 percent of the bill
Nothing, because the tip is included
questions.why_es: Lo habitual es dejar entre 15 y 20 por ciento de la cuenta antes de impuestos.

questions.q: Why should you tell people what is in your dish?
options: Because some guests have allergies or don't eat meat
Because the host needs the recipe
questions.why_es: Algunos invitados tienen alergias o no comen carne, así que es útil saber los ingredientes.
